extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (agents/attorneys), and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for withdrawing a holding of abandonment and for petitioning to revive an abandoned patent application (including required evidence, timing, fees, and special rules by application type and filing date). Covers petitions under 37 CFR 1.181 and 1.137 and related provisions (e.g., 1.8, 1.10, 1.135).

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper RCE does not toll time periods / may effect abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: An RCE filed without the appropriate fee or a submission will be treated as improper; the filing of an RCE will be treated as a withdrawal of the appeal by the applicant. An improper RCE will not operate to toll the running of any time period set in the previous Office action for reply to avoid abandonment. Prior to payment of the issue fee, an allowed application may become abandoned if an RCE is improperly filed without the appropriate fee or a submission; the improper RCE will not toll the time period for payment of the issue fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.114(d) and MPEP § 706.07(h) subsections VI and IX for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: When proceedings are terminated (35 U.S.C. 120 context)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of copendency under 35 U.S.C. 120, a second application is copending with an earlier application only if filed before (i.e., not later than) the patenting, abandonment of, or termination of proceedings on the earlier application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings are terminated in situations including (A) abandonment for failure to pay the issue fee (termination as of the date issue fee was due), (B) losing an interference as to all claims (termination as of the date appeal/review was due if none filed), (C) decision by the Patent Trial and Appeal Board, and (D) decision by the court. See MPEP § 711.02(c) and § 711.03(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration vs. revival — appropriate remedy
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant contends there was no abandonment in fact (e.g., dispute as to sufficiency of reply or controlling dates), applicant may request withdrawal of the holding of abandonment under 37 CFR 1.181(a) (petition to withdraw holding of abandonment) which does not require a fee; if there is no dispute that the application is abandoned, a petition to revive under 37 CFR 1.137 (with appropriate fee) is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition to withdraw a holding is for disputes about the existence of abandonment; petition to revive is for reviving actually abandoned applications. See MPEP § 711.03 and the 'I. PETITION TO WITHDRAW HOLDING OF ABANDONMENT' discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holding based on insufficiency of reply — examiner discretion to reverse
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may deny that a reply was incomplete. The primary examiner, though lacking authority to act on an application with no action by applicant during the reply period, may reverse his or her holding as to whether an amendment received was responsive and then act on the application—this is a determination that the application was never abandoned rather than a revival.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 711.03(a) and also MPEP § 714.03 for related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holding based on failure to reply within period — date disputes may permit reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment reaches the USPTO after expiration of the reply period and dates are undisputed, no reconsideration is possible; however, if examiner and applicant disagree about when the reply period began or ended, the applicant may challenge the holding of abandonment on those grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish undisputed late filings (no relief) from date disputes (may support petition to withdraw holding). See MPEP § 711.03(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment by failure to reply (37 CFR 1.135) — effect and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant fails to reply within the time provided under §§ 1.134 and 1.136, the application will become abandoned unless an Office action indicates otherwise; prosecution to save the application must include a complete and proper reply required by the condition of the application. Admission/refusal to admit amendments after final rejection or non-responsive amendments will not save the application from abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a reply is a bona fide attempt to advance the application and substantially complete but inadvertent omissions occurred, applicant may be given a new time under § 1.134 to supply the omission. See 37 CFR 1.135.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival on basis of unintentional delay (37 CFR 1.137) — core petition requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to revive may be filed if the delay in reply by applicant or patent owner was unintentional. A grantable petition must be accompanied by: (1) the required reply to the outstanding Office action (unless previously filed), (2) the petition fee as set in § 1.17(m), (3) any terminal disclaimer (and fee) required under paragraph (d), and (4) a statement that the entire delay from the due date until filing the grantable petition was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may require additional information when there's a question whether the delay was unintentional. See 37 CFR 1.137(a)-(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the required reply when petitioning to revive (37 CFR 1.137(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviving, the reply must include specific items depending on the cause of abandonment: e.g., for abandonment under § 1.57(a) include copy of specification and drawings of the previously filed application; for abandonment for failure to pay the issue fee include payment of the issue fee or outstanding balance; for failure to prosecute the reply may be met by filing a continuing application or, for certain nonprovisional applications, filing a request for continued examination (RCE) compliant with § 1.114.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the revival reply addresses the specific reason the application became abandoned and includes payments or filings necessary to cure that cause. See 37 CFR 1.137(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer requirement for revival (37 CFR 1.137(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain petitions to revive must be accompanied by a terminal disclaimer and fee: in design applications; in utility or plant applications filed before June 8, 1995 (the terminal part of term dedicated equals the period of abandonment or the period beyond 20 years as described); and such disclaimer must also apply to certain continuing applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (d) also specifies exceptions (e.g., revival sought solely for copendency with post-June-8-1995 applications or for reissue or reexamination). Consult 37 CFR 1.137(d) and MPEP § 711.03(c) subsection II for calculations of the period to be disclaimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for reconsideration of refusal to revive — timing and extension
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for reconsideration or review of a decision refusing to revive an abandoned application must be filed within two months of the decision refusing to revive (or within the time set in the decision). Unless otherwise indicated, this period may be extended under the provisions of relevant sections (e.g., § 1.136 for abandoned applications, § 1.550(c) for certain reexaminations, § 1.956 for certain inter partes reexaminations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.137(e) for details on timing and applicable extension provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival for abandonment due to failure to notify Office of foreign filing (37 CFR 1.137(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprovisional application abandoned pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 122(b)(2)(B)(iii) for failure to timely notify the Office of a foreign filing may be revived pursuant to 37 CFR 1.137; the reply requirement is met by the notification of such foreign filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a petition under this section will not stay any period for reply that may be running against the application. See 37 CFR 1.137(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Revival of provisional applications and their pendency limit (37 CFR 1.137(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application abandoned for failure to timely respond to an Office requirement may be revived pursuant to 37 CFR 1.137, but a provisional application will not be regarded as pending after twelve months from its filing date under any circumstances (subject to 35 U.S.C. 119(e)(3) and § 1.7(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional revival limited by statutory 12‑month pendency rule; use § 1.137(g) guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to the Director under 37 CFR 1.181 — scope and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.181 may be taken to the Director from any action or requirement of an examiner in ex parte prosecution, or in ex parte or inter partes prosecution of a reexamination not subject to appeal to the PTAB or the court; from matters statutorily reserved to the Director; or to invoke supervisory authority in appropriate circumstances. The mere filing of a petition does not stay any period for reply or other proceedings. Petitions not filed within two months of the mailing date of the action/notice may be dismissed as untimely, except as provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.181(a) and (f); for petitions involving PTAB action see § 41.3. Filing a petition is not a stay and untimely petitions may be dismissed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper petition to withdraw holding of abandonment vs. petition to revive — fee consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to withdraw a holding of abandonment under 37 CFR 1.181(a) (where applicant contends application is not abandoned) does not require a fee. When there is no dispute that an application is abandoned and the petition seeks revival, a petition under 37 CFR 1.137 with the appropriate fee is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the correct petition type based on whether the issue is factual dispute of abandonment or an actual abandonment requiring revival; fee only for revival petitions. See MPEP discussion under 'I. PETITION TO WITHDRAW HOLDING OF ABANDONMENT.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to withdraw based on nonreceipt of Office action — showing required (practitioner)
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish nonreceipt of an Office communication, a practitioner must submit a statement describing the system used for recording Office actions received at the correspondence address of record, demonstrate that the docketing system is sufficiently reliable, and provide documentary proof (e.g., application number, attorney docket number, mail date of Office action, due date). A copy of the records used (master docket, file jacket, incoming mail log, calendar, reminder system, individual docket) showing no entry for the Office action is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no master docket exists, provide other evidence such as file jacket, mail log, calendar, reminder system, or individual docket record. See MPEP § 711.03 '1. Showing of Nonreceipt Required of a Practitioner.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to withdraw based on nonreceipt of Office action — showing required (pro se applicant)
rubrics_metrics.description: A pro se petitioner must explain how mail from the USPTO is received and tracked, how patent matters are maintained, where correspondence is kept, how due dates are recorded, and how the petitioner is reminded of response due dates; provide any documentary evidence available and a statement that a search was conducted and the Office action was not found, and that petitioner resided at or routinely checked the correspondence address after the mailing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO recognizes pro se may lack formal docketing, but some explanation and documentary support is required. See MPEP § 711.03 '1. Showing of Nonreceipt Required of a Pro Se Applicant.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to withdraw based on timely mailing/filing evidence — acceptable evidence and processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence that a reply was timely mailed or filed may include Priority Mail Express® deposit (use 37 CFR 1.10 procedures), a postcard receipt properly identifying the reply (provides prima facie evidence), or a certificate of mailing under 37 CFR 1.8. When shown, such replies must be entered in One Patent Service Gateway (via Patent Data Portal) with the Priority Mail Express® date or postcard receipt date or the actual date of receipt for certificate of mailing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relying on certificate of mailing, the attesting statement must be on a personal knowledge basis or otherwise satisfactory to the Director; supporting mailing logs or duplicate copies may be required. See MPEP § 711.03 'B. Petition To Withdraw Holding of Abandonment Based on Evidence That a Reply Was Timely Mailed or Filed' and 37 CFR 1.8/1.10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of untimely petition to withdraw — 2‑month rule and possible terminal disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.181(f), petitions not filed within two months of the mailing date of the action or notice from which relief is requested may be dismissed as untimely (the two‑month period is generally not extendable). Rather than dismissing an untimely petition, the Office may require a terminal disclaimer as a condition of granting an untimely petition to withdraw the holding of abandonment. If record indicates intentional delay, the Office may dismiss solely on that basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider special terminal disclaimer conditions for design or pre‑June‑8‑1995 utility/plant applications (see next items). See 37 CFR 1.181(f) and MPEP § 711.03 'C. Treatment of Untimely Petition To Withdraw Holding of Abandonment.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer and timing rules for design and pre‑June‑8‑1995 applications
rubrics_metrics.description: For design applications and utility/plant applications filed before June 8, 1995: a petition to withdraw a holding of abandonment not filed within two months of the mail date of the notice of abandonment generally will not be treated on its merits unless accompanied by a terminal disclaimer under 37 CFR 1.321(a) and the fee. The period to be disclaimed is the terminal part of the patent term equivalent to the period between (A) two months after the mail date of the notice of abandonment and (B) the filing date of a grantable petition to withdraw.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant never received the notice of abandonment, a 12‑month window from applicant's filing/submission applies (subject to terminal disclaimer) absent extraordinary circumstances. See MPEP § 711.03(c) subsection II.G.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment for utility/plant applications filed on/after June 8, 1995 but before May 29, 2000
rubrics_metrics.description: For utility/plant applications filed on or after June 8, 1995 but before May 29, 2000, a terminal disclaimer should not be required as a condition of granting an untimely petition to withdraw the holding of abandonment; however OPLA consultation is necessary if the holding involves periods during appellate review, interference/derivation proceedings, or sealed/suspended prosecution due to secrecy orders because of patent term adjustment effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult OPLA where petitioner seeks relief involving periods tied to interference/derivation or secrecy orders to properly address potential patent term adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment for applications filed on/after May 29, 2000 — no terminal disclaimer required
rubrics_metrics.description: In utility and plant applications filed on or after May 29, 2000, a terminal disclaimer should not be required as a condition of granting an untimely petition to withdraw the holding of abandonment because patent term adjustment is automatically reduced under 37 CFR 1.704(c)(4) (and if applicant did not receive notice, reduction under 1.704(a) may apply for failure to engage in reasonable efforts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent term adjustment provisions of the AIPA affect whether terminal disclaimers are necessary; apply 37 CFR 1.704 rules accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delgar v. Schuyler principle — nonreceipt allegation may justify withdrawal/remail
rubrics_metrics.description: An allegation, supported by evidence, that an Office action was never received may be considered in a petition to withdraw the holding of abandonment; if adequately supported, the Office may grant withdrawal and remail the Office action. This applies to notices of abandonment and Notices of Allowance (and to abandonment for failure to prosecute or failure to pay issue fee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence must demonstrate nonreceipt (not merely poor recordkeeping), and historical patterns of nonreceipt by practitioner may undermine such a claim. See Delgar v. Schuyler and related case law cited in MPEP § 711.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority Mail Express®, postcard receipts, and certificate of mailing handling rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition relying on Priority Mail Express® must include appropriate 37 CFR 1.10(c),(d),(e),(g) procedures and be entered in One Patent Service Gateway with the Priority Mail Express® date. A postcard receipt identifying the reply is prima facie evidence of timely filing and must be entered with that date. When relying on a certificate of mailing under 37 CFR 1.8, the attesting statement must be on a personal knowledge basis or supported by evidence (e.g., mailing logs) and the duplicate copy is entered with the actual date of receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant does not have to wait until abandonment to notify the Office of a previous mailing; check Patent Center/filing system status before notifying. See MPEP § 711.03(B) and MPEP § 512.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director may require additional information where unintentional delay is questioned
rubrics_metrics.description: When there's a question whether the delay was unintentional in a 37 CFR 1.137 petition, the Director may require additional information beyond the statutory checklist (reply, fee, terminal disclaimer, statement of unintentionality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide comprehensive supporting evidence (timing, mail logs, statements) if there is any doubt about the unintentional nature of the delay. See 37 CFR 1.137(b) and related MPEP commentary.
